name: Bitbucket
summary: Atlassian’s Git host, built to sit next to Jira: pull requests, code review and Bitbucket Pipelines CI, as the Bitbucket Cloud service or the self-managed Bitbucket Data Center.
intro: Bitbucket comes in two products. Bitbucket Cloud, at bitbucket.org, is the hosted service; Bitbucket Data Center is the version you run yourself, the successor of Stash and Bitbucket Server. Both host Git repositories (Mercurial was removed from Cloud in 2020) and review changes as pull requests. Data Center can keep repositories on Bitbucket Mesh, added in 8.0, which replicates each repository across several nodes instead of a shared NFS volume, so losing one node doesn’t make its repositories unavailable.

What sets it apart is Atlassian’s other products. Put a Jira work item key such as `JRA-34` in a branch name, commit message or pull request title and the work item links to it; Smart Commits go further, so `JRA-34 #time 2h #comment fixed #resolve` in a commit message logs time, comments and moves the item through its workflow. Bitbucket Pipelines, its built-in CI, reads `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` from the root of the repository and runs each step in a Docker container in Atlassian’s cloud; a `pull-requests` pipeline first merges the destination branch into the source branch, so it tests the result of the merge. Since April 2026 Pipelines can also run AI agent steps through Atlassian’s Rovo Dev, in open beta.

Cloud is free for up to 5 users with 50 build minutes a month, then $3.65 per user a month for Standard and $8 for Premium, which adds enforced merge checks, IP allowlisting and deployment permissions. A Cloud repository should stay under 2 GB and stops accepting new commits at 4 GB. Atlassian ended support for its Server products on February 15, 2024, and in September 2025 announced that its other Data Center products reach end of life on March 28, 2029; Bitbucket Data Center is exempt and continues, with a hybrid license covering both Data Center and Cloud. The latest Data Center release is 10.5 (September 29, 2026), and 10.2 is the current long-term support version.
strengths: The tightest link to Jira: a work item key in a branch, commit or pull request links them, and Smart Commits update work items from commit messages
Cheap per user, with CI included: $3.65 per user a month on Standard, and Pipelines minutes shared across the workspace
Still self-hostable: Bitbucket Data Center continues after Atlassian’s 2029 Data Center end of life, with Mesh for replicated storage
Pull request pipelines test the merge with the destination branch, not just the branch on its own
limits: Small hard limits: a Cloud repository stops accepting new commits at 4 GB, and a Free workspace gets 1 GB of repository storage in total
The Free plan stops at 5 users and 50 build minutes a month; enforced merge checks need Premium
Self-hosting now means Data Center: Server licenses lost support on February 15, 2024
Pull requests from forks don’t trigger pull request pipelines, and AI agent steps need a separate Rovo Dev license

story: Bitbucket began as an independent hosting service for Mercurial repositories, run by its co-founder and CEO Jesper Nøhr. When Atlassian bought it on September 29, 2010 it had more than 60,000 accounts. Atlassian switched it to pricing per user with unlimited repositories, free for up to 5 users with private repositories, and said it would stay neutral about version control. A year later, on October 3, 2011, Bitbucket added Git repositories next to Mercurial ones.

For companies that wanted Git behind their own firewall, Atlassian released Stash 1.0 on May 1, 2012, and renamed it Bitbucket Server with version 4.0 on September 21, 2015. Meanwhile Git won: in August 2019 Atlassian announced it would remove Mercurial from Bitbucket Cloud, because fewer than 1% of new Bitbucket users chose it. New Mercurial repositories were blocked from February 1, 2020, and every Mercurial repository was disabled on August 26, 2020.

Atlassian then pushed customers toward its cloud. Server products lost support on February 15, 2024, and on September 8, 2025 Atlassian set the end of life of its Data Center products for March 28, 2029. Bitbucket was the exception: Bitbucket Data Center continues, and its customers get a hybrid license that also covers Bitbucket Cloud.

choices.choice: Start with Mercurial, then go Git-only
choices.why: Bitbucket was the main host for Mercurial when Atlassian bought it. By 2019 under 1% of new users picked Mercurial, while Stack Overflow’s 2018 survey had almost 90% of developers on Git, and Atlassian decided supporting two systems split its engineering effort.

Atlassian sells Bitbucket as part of a suite. Work item keys in branches, commits and pull requests link code to Jira, and Smart Commits let developers comment, log time and change a work item’s status without leaving Git.

choices.choice: Keep a self-managed Bitbucket after all
choices.why: Atlassian retired Server in 2024 and is retiring Data Center for Jira, Confluence and its other products by 2029, but it exempted Bitbucket Data Center and offered a hybrid license, so customers can keep source code on their own machines.
